tests/scripts/test_issue_4369_delivery_lifecycle.py-105-108: 1

`105-108`: ** Trivial** · **Functional Correctness** · **Low value** **Unverified finding** Verification ran but could not confirm this finding. It is shown for review, not as a verified issue. **Compare timestamps as parsed datetimes, not strings.** Line 108 uses `min(candidates, key=lambda run: run["created_at"])`, which compares ISO strings. Line 188 compares `inventory["start"] <= run["created_at"] <= inventory["end"]` the same way. Lexicographic order matches chronological order only when every value uses the same format and UTC suffix. Other places in this file already parse values with `datetime.fromisoformat`. Parse these values the same way, so a format difference, such as an offset or fractional seconds, cannot give a false pass. Line 105 also compares `producer["createdAt"]`, which ends in `Z`. `datetime.fromisoformat` accepts `Z` from Python 3.11. The repository requires Python 3.13 or later, so this is safe.
Proposed fix

```diff - assert min(candidates, key=lambda run: run["created_at"])["id"] == following["id"] == FOLLOWING + earliest = min(candidates, key=lambda run: datetime.fromisoformat(run["created_at"])) + assert earliest["id"] == following["id"] == FOLLOWING ```
